problemText: Lines m and n are parallel and are cut by transversal t. Two of the eight angles formed both lie between m and n and are on the SAME side of t. What must be true of these two angles?
choices: There is not enough information to tell.
hints: Both angles are interior and on the same side of the transversal — that describes one specific named pair.
Same-side interior angles are supplementary when the lines are parallel: they add to 180°, they are not equal.

problemText: Lines r and s are parallel and are cut by transversal t. An interior angle at the crossing with r measures 73°. What is the measure of the interior angle at the crossing with s that lies on the same side of t?
hints: Both angles are interior and on the same side of t, so classify the pair before computing.
Same-side interior angles are supplementary with r ∥ s, so subtract: 180 - 73.

problemText: Lines a and b are parallel and are cut by a transversal. A pair of alternate exterior angles measures (5x - 4)° and (3x + 16)°. What is the value of x?
hints: Alternate exterior angles are congruent when the lines are parallel — set the two expressions equal, do not add them.
5x - 4 = 3x + 16 gives 2x = 20. The question asks for x, not for the angle measure.

problemText: Lines j and k are parallel and are cut by transversal t. Two interior angles on the same side of t measure (3x + 14)° and (5x - 26)°. What is the measure of the LARGER of these two angles?
hints: Same-side interior angles are supplementary with j ∥ k, so the two expressions ADD to 180.
(3x + 14) + (5x - 26) = 180 gives 8x = 192, so x = 24. Now evaluate both expressions and pick the larger measure.

problemText: Lines p and q are parallel and are cut by transversal t. An angle at the crossing with p measures (2x + 30)°. At the crossing with q, the angle corresponding to it forms a linear pair with an angle measuring 96°. What is the value of x?
hints: Work the crossing with q first: a linear pair is supplementary, so that corresponding angle measures 180 - 96.
Corresponding angles are congruent with p ∥ q, so 2x + 30 = 84.

problemText: Lines m and n are parallel and are cut by transversal t, with m the upper line and n the lower line. The interior angle at the crossing with m on the right side of t measures (5x - 8)°. At the crossing with n, the interior angle on the right side of t forms a linear pair with an angle measuring (3x + 12)°. Find the value of x and type your answer as a number.
hints: Handle the crossing with n first: a linear pair is supplementary, so that interior angle measures 180 - (3x + 12), which simplifies to 168 - 3x.
The two interior angles on the right side of t form a same-side interior pair, so they ADD to 180: (5x - 8) + (168 - 3x) = 180.

problemText: Two lines are cut by a transversal, and a pair of alternate interior angles is congruent. Which reason lets you conclude that the two lines are parallel?
choices: Converse of the Alternate Interior Angles Theorem
Converse of the Same-Side Interior Angles Theorem
hints: You are reasoning FROM an angle fact TO parallel, which is the converse direction.
The forward theorem starts by assuming the lines are parallel, so it cannot be used to prove them parallel.

problemText: Lines e and f are cut by transversal t, with e the upper line and f the lower line. The angle below e and to the right of t measures 118°, and the angle above f and to the right of t measures 62°. Which conclusion is correct?
choices: e ∥ f, by the Converse of the Alternate Interior Angles Theorem
e and f are not parallel, because the two angles are not congruent
e ∥ f, by the Converse of the Same-Side Interior Angles Theorem
No conclusion is possible without a third angle measure
hints: The strip between e and f is the interior region: below e and above f are both interior positions, and both angles are on the right of t.
A same-side interior pair certifies parallel when the measures are supplementary — check whether 118 + 62 = 180.

problemText: In a plane, line g and line h are each perpendicular to line t. Which conclusion follows, and for what reason?
choices: g ⊥ h, by the definition of perpendicular lines
Nothing follows, because perpendicularity says nothing about parallelism
g ∥ t, by the Perpendicular Transversal Converse
g ∥ h, by the Perpendicular Transversal Converse
hints: Both right angles sit at crossings with t, so t is playing the role of the transversal and g and h are the two lines being tested.
Two coplanar lines that are each ⊥ to the same line are parallel to each other — this is why square-cut studs off one plate come out parallel.

problemText: Lines c and d are cut by transversal t. The interior angle at the crossing with c on the LEFT side of t measures (7x - 30)°, and the interior angle at the crossing with d on the RIGHT side of t measures (4x + 12)°. What value of x forces c ∥ d?
hints: Both angles are interior and they sit on opposite sides of t, so the pair is alternate interior — that converse wants the measures EQUAL.
7x - 30 = 4x + 12 gives 3x = 42. If you added the expressions to 180 you were using the wrong converse.

problemText: Lines m and n are cut by transversal t, with m the upper line and n the lower line. The angle above m and to the left of t measures 74°, and the angle above n and to the right of t measures 106°. Are m and n parallel, and why?
choices: Yes — by the Converse of the Corresponding Angles Postulate applied directly to the two given angles
No — the two given angles are not congruent, so no converse applies
Yes — vertical angles move the 74° measure to the interior on the right of t, and 74 + 106 = 180, so the Converse of the Same-Side Interior Angles Theorem applies
Yes — by the Converse of the Alternate Exterior Angles Theorem applied directly to the two given angles
hints: Place each angle first: above m is exterior, while above n is between the lines and therefore interior. Mixed positions are not yet a named pair.
At the crossing with m, the vertical angle of the 74° angle sits below m on the right of t and also measures 74° — now both angles are interior and on the same side of t.

problemText: Lines p and q are cut by transversal t, with p the upper line and q the lower line. At the crossing with p, the angle above p and to the right of t measures (4x + 9)°. At the crossing with q, the angle above q and to the right of t forms a linear pair with an angle measuring (2x + 3)°. Find the value of x that makes p ∥ q, and type your answer as a number.
hints: Get the angle at q first: a linear pair is supplementary, so that angle measures 180 - (2x + 3), which simplifies to 177 - 2x.
Above the line and on the right of t is the same position at each crossing, so the pair is corresponding and its converse wants the measures equal: 4x + 9 = 177 - 2x.

problemText: A line has slope 3/8. What is the slope of every line perpendicular to it?
hints: Perpendicular slopes are negative reciprocals — two moves, not one: flip the fraction AND change the sign.
Check your answer by multiplying it with 3/8; the product must be -1.

problemText: Are the lines 4x - y = 9 and y = -4x + 2 parallel, perpendicular, or neither?
hints: Solve the first equation for y before comparing anything: 4x - y = 9 becomes y = 4x - 9.
The slopes are 4 and -4. Opposite signs alone is not enough — the fraction must also be flipped, and (4)(-4) = -16, not -1.

problemText: Which equation describes the line that is parallel to y = (2/5)x - 3 and passes through the point (10, 2)?
hints: Parallel copies the slope unchanged: m = 2/5. The given point then decides the y-intercept.
Substitute (10, 2) into y = (2/5)x + b: 2 = 4 + b. The y-coordinate 2 is not itself the intercept.

problemText: Which equation describes a line that is parallel to 3x - 6y = 18?
hints: Solve 3x - 6y = 18 for y first — in Ax + By = C the slope is not A.
The given line is y = (1/2)x - 3. One choice has the correct slope but is that same line rewritten, and a line is not parallel to itself: parallel lines need equal slopes and DIFFERENT y-intercepts.

problemText: Line k passes through the points (-2, 7) and (4, -5). Which equation describes the line that is perpendicular to k and passes through the point (6, 1)?
hints: Find the slope of k from the two points: m = (-5 - 7)/(4 - (-2)).
Line k has slope -2, so the perpendicular slope is 1/2. Substitute (6, 1) into y = (1/2)x + b and solve for b.

problemText: Line j has equation 5x + 2y = 14. Line k is perpendicular to line j and passes through the point (-5, 3). Type the y-intercept of line k as a number.
hints: Solve 5x + 2y = 14 for y before reading any slope: in Ax + By = C the slope is not A.
Line j has slope -5/2, so line k has slope 2/5. Substitute (-5, 3) into y = (2/5)x + b and solve for b.
